summary: Angora Ridge lookout above Fallen Leaf Lake: NHLR dates it to 1914, a plaque to 1924; unstaffed in the 2007 Angora Fire; closed, still standing.

facts.design: Ground-level buildings (NHLR counts three built over the years, all kept original designs); plaque says the current lookout was built by the CCC in 1935 on forester Coert duBois's design
facts.status_note: NHLR says closed but still standing; a 2009 FFLA list calls the site abandoned; no source read after 2010 describes its condition
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

access.note: NHLR says the lookout is closed. Angora Ridge Road (Forest Road 1214) is seasonal, typically mid-May to mid-November; the Forest Service says the lookout can be accessed seasonally from it. Sources read do not say whether the buildings are open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: Reached from Highway 89 via Fallen Leaf Road, Tahoe Mountain Road and Forest Road 1214; seasonal. NHLR says the lookout is closed, so visitors should stay off the structures.

events.note: NHLR build year and first-service date; Read the Plaque dates the first lookout to 1924 (see resolved_conflicts)
Original lookout per Read the Plaque; later converted into a small residence
Lookout Waterhouse reported from Angora Lookout in a 1925 district newsletter item
Clisby Loomis named as Forest Service lookout at Angora in a 1931 Mountain Democrat item
Civilian Conservation Corps built the current lookout structure
Garage next to the parking lot built some time in the 1940s
Lightning made two direct hits on the lookout tower; no one injured and the steel tower not damaged
Registered May 29, 2003 as NHLR US 518, CA 56
Angora Fire started June 24, 2007 near the unstaffed lookout, which almost succumbed; about 3,100 acres burned and 254 structures destroyed (the structures were not the lookout)
2009 FFLA status list marks the site Abandoned and unstaffed during the 2007 fire
June 2010 photo captions show two lookout structures and a garage on the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 1914 as the year the site first went into service; the plaque dates the original lookout to 1924 and ties 1914 to duBois's idea for fire lookouts. The story reports both.
NHLR describes three ground-level buildings and no steel tower; a 1965 newspaper item describes a steel tower. The sources read do not say when a tower stood or was removed.
NHLR says the lookout is closed; the Forest Service says it can be accessed seasonally from the road. The story reports both: a closed lookout, seasonal road access.

notes_for_editor: Build date conflicts: NHLR says 1914 (first service); the plaque says the original lookout was built in 1924 and the current structure by the CCC in 1935. The story reports both. Registry conflict, not in the story: the firelookout.org California list (https://firelookout.org/lookouts/us/ca/) gives NHLR US 1180, CA 115 at 38.88230, -120.05465, while NHLR's own page gives US 518, CA 56. The brief's number matches NHLR and was kept. No source read describes the buildings after the June 2010 photo captions, so the current condition is unknown; closed/standing rests on NHLR's undated description. Access is inferred from the Forest Service road page, which does not say whether the buildings are open. No photos added: the Weebly captions cite a July 1941 National Archives photo and June 2010 photos by Ron Kemnow, but give no image URLs. OpenStreetMap way 905267264 (Angora Fire Lookout, tower:type observation) was checked but not used. Budget: 9 distinct pages read against a 6-page budget (the CEQAnet and Forest Service pages were needed for the fire date and access), plus 2 web searches.
